analysis.investment_thesis: Paras has real niche capabilities in space optics and EMP shielding with India's defense indigenization as a genuine tailwind, but at 88.8x P/E with FCF/Net Income of only 16% (INR 10 Cr FCF vs INR 61 Cr net profit in FY25), the price demands perfection that the underlying economics cannot yet justify. A 15.6% ROCE business simply does not deserve a 61x EV/EBITDA multiple.
key_strengths: Genuine niche moat in precision defense optics, EMP shielding, and space structures — rare capabilities not easily replicated by generalists
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.08, total debt just INR 24 Cr) with strong FY25 revenue acceleration (+44% YoY to INR 365 Cr)
India's Make-in-India defense push is a structural, multi-decade tailwind with defensible order pipelines from Indian military
key_risks: Atrocious FCF quality — FCF of INR 10 Cr vs net profit of INR 61 Cr in FY25 (16% conversion) signals severe working capital drag or aggressive revenue recognition on long-cycle defense contracts
Single-customer concentration risk inherent to Indian defense contractors; government order delays directly collapse revenue and margins as seen in FY24 profit dip (INR 36→30 Cr)
Valuation offers zero margin of safety — at 88.8x P/E and 61.3x EV/EBITDA, any earnings miss or order slowdown would cause catastrophic price correction
red_flags: FCF/Net Income = 16% in FY25 — earnings quality fails the 80% threshold badly; OCF swung from -INR 46 Cr (FY24) to +INR 45 Cr (FY25), a volatility pattern inconsistent with a 'compounding machine'
ROE of 11.5% is below the cost of equity for a mid-cap Indian defense stock — the market is paying 9.7x book for sub-par returns on equity
Capex scaling fast (INR 35 Cr in FY25 vs INR 26 Cr FY24) while FCF remains anemic — capital consumption not translating to proportional earnings power
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Paras is a small but genuinely differentiated defense technology company — INR 365 Cr revenue, niche capabilities in Zerodur mirrors, diffractive gratings, EMP chambers, and space structures. These are not commodities. However, Munger's first rule is to invert: what must be true for this investment to work at 88.8x P/E? The company must sustain 25%+ earnings growth for a decade with dramatically improving FCF conversion. The FY25 net profit doubling (INR 30→61 Cr) looks impressive, but OCF was only INR 45 Cr and FCF a paltry INR 10 Cr — suggesting high receivables/WIP locked in long-duration defense contracts. ROCE at 15.6% barely clears my 15% hurdle and ROE at 11.5% is definitively below it. I am not paying 88x for mediocre capital returns, regardless of sector narrative.

The defense indigenization story is real — India's defense budget is rising and import substitution is policy. But the market has already priced in 10 years of optimism into the stock. Market cap of INR 6,521 Cr against revenue of INR 365 Cr (P/S of 17.8x) is the market paying for hope, not earnings. Promoter holding of 53.2% is the one genuinely comforting signal — skin in the game matters. But even honest management cannot conjure returns from a business purchased at this multiple. I would revisit at P/E closer to 30-35x (implying a ~60% price decline), where the niche moat and sector tailwinds might earn a reasonable return for a patient investor.
